project.objective: Did Mary E. McAndrew (G13G-P68) and her husband John Mogan of Detroit have any children besides the five already in the tree?

questions.question: Did Mary E. McAndrew (G13G-P68) and her husband John Mogan of Detroit, Michigan, have any children beyond those currently documented in the family tree?
questions.rationale: This is a completeness question requiring exhaustive search of Detroit-area records spanning the probable birth years of any children (approximately 1875–1910). Detroit city birth registrations began 1867; Michigan death records frequently name parents and can surface children not found in birth registers. The five known tree children provide hooks for obituary cross-references that may name additional siblings. Census records (1880–1930) showing the Mogan household will enumerate children present at each decade. City directories and naturalization records may corroborate. Exhaustive negative evidence across these record classes is required before a 'no additional children' conclusion can be drawn.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Searched all accessible FamilySearch collections relevant to Wayne County, Michigan, 1867–1920: census (1880, 1900, 1910, 1920), Michigan State Census 1894, Michigan County Births 1867–1917 (multiple collections), Michigan Deaths 1867–1897, Michigan Births and Christenings 1775–1995, Michigan Church Records (col. 2787825), Michigan Naturalization Records, Michigan Obituaries (FamilySearch col. 2215693), FAN obituaries for all 5 known Mogan children, and original birth register image for Martin Magin. One additional child confirmed: Martin Magin (b. 24 Sep 1887, Detroit), with parentage established by an original registered birth record listing father John Magan and mother Mary. The 1900 census (wife's row) records 7 children born and 6 living as of June 1900 — consistent with 5 tree children + Martin + 1 child who died in infancy. Michigan Deaths 1897–1902 (Ancestry/Michiganology) is inaccessible autonomously and documented as a limitation; it cannot change the confirmed finding of Martin as an additional child, though it would clarify Martin's fate and the 7-born arithmetic. All accessible FamilySearch sources have been searched and are exhausted.

Two independent record types (birth register + census) converge on Martin as a child of John Mogan and Mary McAndrew.

stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: RESOLVED — The 1900 census shows John's row with '7 born / 5 living' and Mary's row with '7 born / 6 living.' Mary's fertility figures are authoritative (the 1900 census columns are addressed to the wife). The 7-born/6-living count is consistent with 5 tree children + Martin + 1 child who died in infancy: a total of 7 born, with 1 having predeceased Mary, leaving 6 living. Martin's absence from the 1900 census household at age 12 is unexplained but consistent with living elsewhere (boarding, relatives, school) or having died 1897–1900. No unresolved conflict blocks the core finding.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: LOW for the core finding — Martin Magin as a 6th child is confirmed by original birth records and cannot be overturned by any unsearched source. MODERATE for completeness: Michigan Deaths 1897–1902 (Ancestry/Michiganology, inaccessible) would clarify whether Martin died before June 1900 and whether the '7 born/6 living' arithmetic implies a 7th yet-unknown child. If Martin died 1897–1900, there would be a living 6th child still unidentified; if Martin was alive in June 1900 but residing elsewhere, the count is fully reconciled with 5 tree children + Martin + 1 infant death. A human researcher with Ancestry access should search Wayne County Michigan death records 1897–1902 for Martin Magin/Magan to resolve this uncertainty.

items.rationale: The 1880 US Federal Census (FamilySearch, free, indexed) lists all household members by name, age, birthplace, and relationship to head. It is the earliest available census that explicitly records relationships, so it will enumerate Mogan children present at home by 1880, covering births roughly from the late 1860s onward. Search head of household John Mogan in Wayne County, Michigan. Cross-check that Mary E. McAndrew appears as wife and note every child enumerated.

The 1890 US Federal Census was destroyed by fire and is unavailable nationwide. The 1894 Michigan State Census (FamilySearch col. 1825187, 381,961 records, index only; also on Ancestry) fills this decade gap and will show the Mogan household mid-decade, capturing children born between 1880 and 1900 who may have left home by the time of the 1900 federal census. Essential for bridging the 10-year census void.

The 1900 US Federal Census (FamilySearch, free, indexed) is the single most important census for this completeness question: it includes a column recording the number of children BORN to the mother and the number STILL LIVING as of 1900. This gives a quantified baseline against which to measure the known five tree children. It also lists all children at home in 1900, provides birth months and years, and may show nearby Mogan households of married children. Search John Mogan in Wayne County, Michigan; note the children-born/living figures for Mary.

The 1910 US Federal Census (FamilySearch, free, indexed) shows the Mogan household a decade after 1900. Adult children will have formed their own households (possibly in the same Detroit neighborhood); younger children born after 1900 will still be at home. Cross-referencing the 1900 children-born count with who appears in 1910 helps identify any child who died 1900-1910. Also search neighbors for nearby Mogan households that could be married children.

The 1920 US Federal Census (FamilySearch, free, indexed) captures the household near the end of the probable child-birth range. Any children born in the early 1900s still living at home would appear here; if Mary E. McAndrew is widowed or living with a married child, that enumeration may reveal a previously unknown child. Note: Detroit streets were renumbered on 1 January 1921, so 1920 census addresses use pre-renumbering numbers that differ from post-1921 records.

Michigan Obituaries (FamilySearch col. 2215693, 8.9M records, indexed + images, covering 1890-2003) covers Detroit-area newspapers. Obituaries for Mary E. McAndrew and John Mogan are the highest-yield single source for a complete child list: standard obituary convention in this era named all surviving sons and daughters (and sometimes predeceased ones). Search 'Mogan' and 'McAndrew' with Wayne County / Detroit residence. Also check GenealogyBank Michigan Newspaper Archives 1817-1999 as a complementary source.

Search father's name John Mogan and mother's name Mary McAndrew/Mogan across the full period 1867-1917. A separate Ancestry search (item 8) is required for Detroit city proper births.

This is potentially a complete child enumeration in a single document. Search John Mogan in both collections.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Additional Children of John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew, Detroit, Michigan

**Question:** Did Mary E. McAndrew (G13G-P68) and her husband John Mogan (GQWY-3JF) of Detroit, Michigan, have any children beyond those previously documented in the family tree — Anna Irene, Edward Lawrence, Thomas Frank, John Vincent, and Mary L. Mogan?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of available evidence establishes that John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew had at least one child not previously in the family tree: **Martin Magin (later Mogan), born 24 September 1887 in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan.** This conclusion rests on an original registered birth record confirmed by direct image examination. The 1900 United States census fertility data indicates that Mary bore seven children in total, of whom six were living in June 1900; this arithmetic is consistent with the five children already in the tree plus Martin, with one child having died in infancy or early childhood. The evidence does not identify any seventh child, and the possibility of an additional, unidentified child cannot be entirely ruled out pending access to Michigan death records for 1897–1902 (held on Ancestry.com, not accessible in this investigation).

---

### Birth Register Evidence

The primary evidence for Martin Magin is his registration in the Wayne County birth register. The FamilySearch indexed entry — "Michigan, County Births, 1867-1917," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QLT2-G99Q : accessed 6 August 2026), entry for Martin Magin and John Magan, 24 Sep 1887; citing Wayne County, Michigan, county clerk records — records the child as Martin Magin, male, born 24 September 1887 in Detroit; father John Magan (occupation: Engineer); mother Mary.

The underlying original birth register image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-8BZF-3GX) was transcribed directly. Entry #93, on a Detroit Ward 8 page covering 1887–1888, confirms: child Martin Magin, male; address 1806; father John Magan, birthplace *Mich*; mother Mary, birthplace blank; father's occupation Engineer. No other Mogan, Magan, or Magin children appear on the fourteen-entry page.

The father's birthplace is recorded as *Mich* (Michigan) in this register, which conflicts with evidence from multiple other sources showing John Mogan as Irish-born — confirmed by the 1900 federal census ("United States, Census, 1900," FamilySearch, ARK ark:/61903/1:1:M91M-LKB), the 1877 birth registration for John Vincent Mogan, and the Find A Grave memorial. This discrepancy is best explained as a clerical error by the register official. All other attributes align with the known family: name *John Magan* (a common indexing variant of Mogan in this record series), male, Detroit, married, contemporary with the 1887 birth event.

The birth register is an original record created at the time of the event with the parents as informants. The parentage assertions — that Martin Magin was the child of John Magan and Mary — carry primary information quality and direct evidence type. They are the strongest evidence class available for this conclusion.

### Corroborating Birth Register Pattern

The registration of John Vincent Mogan on 12 May 1877 in the same series — "Michigan, County Births, 1867-1917," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGYQ-QXMZ : accessed 2026-08-06), entry for John V Mogan and John Mogan, 12 May 1877 — lists father John Mogan and mother Mary Mogan (birthplace New Brunswick). This confirms that the couple's children were registered in this series, that surname variants Magan/Mogan are used interchangeably across entries, and that *Mary* is the mother's given name in both registrations. Martin's registration fits the established documentary pattern for this family.

Martin Magin also appears in "Michigan, Births, 1867-1902" (FamilySearch col. 1459684) and "Michigan, Births and Christenings, 1775-1995" (col. 1675348), both derived from the same Wayne County register. These are derivative corroborations, not independent sources.

### 1900 Census Fertility Figures

The 1900 United States census, "United States, Census, 1900," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M91M-LKB : accessed 2026-08-06), entry for John Magan household, Detroit Ward 8, Wayne County, Michigan; citing NARA microfilm publication T623, roll 734, records on Mary E. Magan's row: **children born = 7, children living = 6** as of June 1900. Three children appear in this household — Annie I, Edward L, and Mary L. John's row records 7 born and 5 living; the discrepancy between the husband's and wife's figures is common in this census, and the wife's column is the standard fertility record.

With five tree children and Martin Magin identified (six children total), the 7-born/6-living figure is consistent with two interpretations:

1. **Martin was alive in June 1900 but residing elsewhere** — at age 12 he could have been boarding, at school, or staying with relatives. In this case: 6 living = 5 tree children + Martin; 7 born = these 6 + 1 child who died in infancy or early childhood (unrecorded or not found).
2. **Martin died between 1897 and June 1900** — Michigan Deaths 1867–1897 (FamilySearch col. 1452402) returned no result for Martin, confirming he survived past 1897. In this case: 6 living = 5 tree children + 1 unidentified sixth child; 7 born = 5 tree + Martin + 1 unidentified child.

Searches of the 1900 census nationally failed to locate Martin Magin in any household, leaving his status at the census date uncertain. Neither interpretation can be confirmed without the Michigan death records for 1897–1902 (Ancestry/Michiganology, not accessible in this investigation).

### 1920 Census and Scope of Research

The 1920 census — "United States, Census, 1920," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MZW8-V4G : accessed 2026-08-06), entry for Mary E Mogan in household of John L Mogan, Detroit Ward 10, Wayne County, Michigan, 1920; citing NARA microfilm publication T625 — shows Mary E. Mogan (widowed, b. ~1855, New Brunswick) residing in the Detroit household of her son John L. Mogan (identified as John Vincent Mogan, 9XPJ-TRP, at probable confidence). Also in that household: Mary Mogan (female, b. ~1889, Michigan, single), identified as Mary L. Mogan (LZ18-RZM), a known tree child. No previously unknown children appear.

In addition to the records cited above, searches for additional children were conducted across: Michigan State Census 1894 (FamilySearch col. 1825187), Michigan Church Records (col. 2787825), Michigan Naturalization Records (col. 2546149), Michigan Obituaries (col. 2215693) for both parents, and FAN obituaries for all five known Mogan children. None named a child not already in the tree or identified as Martin Magin. The 1880, 1910, and 1920 U.S. federal censuses were also searched. These searches are documented in the research log (log_009 through log_046).

### Assessment and Tier

The evidence strongly suggests that John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew had at least one child beyond the five previously in the family tree — Martin Magin, born 24 September 1887 in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan, established by an original registered birth record and confirmed by image examination. This conclusion is assessed at the **probable** tier rather than proved because the full enumeration of children cannot be certified while Michigan death records for 1897–1902 remain inaccessible, leaving open the question of Martin's fate in 1900 and, derivatively, whether a seventh child existed and remains unidentified. A human researcher with Ancestry.com access should search Wayne County, Michigan, death records 1897–1902 for *Martin Magin* or *Martin Magan* to resolve this uncertainty. If Martin is found to have survived past June 1900, the 7-born/6-living count is fully accounted for and the finding would approach proved; if he died before June 1900, a sixth living child in 1900 may remain to be identified.

# Locality Guide: Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan (1867–1915)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Wayne County organized November 21, 1815, as an original county. Detroit re-established as a city in 1805 after the fire.
- **County seat:** Detroit
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Michigan (state since January 26, 1837)
- **Population during period:** Population data unavailable from the survey tool at city level. Detroit was a major industrial city during this period, growing substantially from the 1870s through the early 20th century.
- **Economy:** Manufacturing, shipping/Great Lakes commerce, auto industry emerging by 1900–1910. Heavy immigrant working-class population.
- **Ethnic composition:** Large Irish, German, Polish, and later Southern/Eastern European immigrant communities. Irish Catholics commonly found throughout this period.
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (largest single denomination, Archdiocese of Detroit); Methodist, Episcopal, Presbyterian, Lutheran.
- **Key historical events:** Post-Civil War industrialization; auto industry emergence c.1899–1910; massive immigration waves; significant annexation of surrounding communities 1806–1926.

## Boundary changes
- Detroit city boundaries expanded continuously 1806–1926 through annexation; many neighborhood names that appear in early records (e.g., Springwells, Delray, Hamtramck) were independent communities that were later absorbed. Records for these areas may appear under the suburb name, not Detroit.
- Wayne County boundaries have been stable during the target period; no county boundary changes affect this research.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Statewide county registration began 1867; general compliance achieved by c.1915 (1905 law).
- **Births:** FamilySearch col. 1459684 (Michigan Births, 1867-1902) — **indexed + images**; col. 1923472 (Michigan County Births, 1867-1917) — **indexed + images** for Wayne County outside Detroit; col. 1675348 (Michigan Births and Christenings, 1775-1995) — **index only**. Ancestry has Michigan Birth Records 1867-1913 (index & images, subscription).
- **Deaths:** FamilySearch col. 1452402 (Michigan Deaths, 1867-1897) — **indexed + images**; col. 1675357 (Michigan Deaths and Burials, 1800-1995) — **index only**. Ancestry has Michigan Death Records 1867-1952 and 1897-1929 (subscription).
- **Marriages:** FamilySearch col. 1452395 (Michigan Marriages, 1868-1925) — **indexed + images**; col. 1810350 (Michigan County Marriages, 1820-1941) — **indexed + images**; col. 2473289 (Michigan County Marriages Index, 1820-1937) — **indexed + images**.
- **CRITICAL GAP:** FamilySearch's Wayne County birth/death collections explicitly exclude City of Detroit records. Detroit city births (since 1893) → Wayne County Clerk's Office. Detroit city deaths (since 1897) → Detroit Health Department (1151 Taylor St, Detroit, MI 48202, tel. 313-876-4133). Wayne County marriage returns 1803-1893 are originals at the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library.
- **Gaps:** Pre-1867 civil registration does not exist; 1867-1904 records may be incomplete due to uneven compliance.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (largest), Methodist, Episcopal, Lutheran, Presbyterian.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, first communions.
- **Where held:** Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Detroit records (1704-1930) on microfilm at Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library. FamilySearch col. 2787825 (Michigan Church Records, 1819-1991) — indexed + images; col. 2515887 (Michigan Church Marriages, 1865-1931) — indexed + images.
- **Priority for McAndrew/Mogan research:** Irish-surnamed families in Detroit were overwhelmingly Roman Catholic. The Archdiocesan microfilm collection at Burton Historical should be checked for baptisms, marriages, and burials that may not appear in civil records.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1870, 1880 (all members listed), 1900, 1910, 1920 — all indexed and available on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry ($). The 1890 census was destroyed by fire. Starting in 1880, relationships to head of household are recorded.
- **State census:** 1894 Michigan State Census — FamilySearch col. 1825187 — **index only** (381,961 records). Also on Ancestry ($).
- **Mortality schedules:** FamilySearch col. 2632078 (1850-1880) — indexed + images.
- **Note:** The census years 1880, 1900, 1910 are the most productive for enumerating children in the Mogan household during the probable birth span 1875-1910.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch col. 2013878 (Michigan Probate Records, 1797-1973) — **BROWSE-ONLY images** (4.7M images, no name index). Ancestry has Michigan Wills and Probate Records, 1784-1980 — **indexed + images** ($). Physical originals at Wayne County Probate Court, Coleman A. Young Municipal Center, Detroit.
- **Research value:** Wills of parents and known children frequently name siblings and relatives not found in vital records.

### Land records
- **System:** Rectangular survey (federal land state).
- **Where held:** Wayne County Register of Deeds (online at waynecountylandrecords.com); FamilySearch full-text land records search.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Civil War (1861-1865), Spanish-American War (1898), WWI (1917-1918).
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, WWI draft registration cards.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch has Michigan Military Discharge Records (col. 4123955) and WWI draft cards (col. 2999489, indexed + images). Ancestry has Spanish-American War and Civil War Michigan records.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Elmwood, Woodmere, Mt. Elliott, Holy Sepulchre (Catholic), and various denominational cemeteries.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves (both searchable via FamilySearch). FamilySearch col. 3264363 (Michigan GAR Cemetery Index, 1799-1999) — indexed + images.
- **Physical records:** Burton Historical Collection holds cemetery transcription guides.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Detroit Free Press (1831–present), Detroit Evening News/Detroit News, Detroit Journal. Major Irish-community papers also existed.
- **Where held:** Chronicling America (LOC) has digitized Michigan newspapers; GenealogyBank has Michigan Newspaper Archives 1817-1999; Ancestry/Newspapers.com for Detroit papers. Burton Historical Collection has extensive physical newspaper holdings.
- **Content value:** Obituaries are critical — they frequently list all surviving children by name and sometimes children who predeceased the subject. FamilySearch Michigan Obituaries (col. 2215693, 8.9M records, 1890-2003) is **indexed + images** and is an essential first search.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Detroit (overland via Windsor, Ontario, Canada); also New York, Baltimore, Quebec for earlier arrivals.
- **Record types:** Manifests of Arrivals at Port of Detroit 1906-1956 (FamilySearch col. 1916040 — indexed + images, 1.36M records); US Border Crossings from Canada 1894-1954 (FamilySearch col. 2185932).
- **Naturalization:** FamilySearch col. 2546149 (Michigan Naturalization Records, 1837-1997) — indexed + images, 2.1M records; col. 2110745 (Michigan Eastern District Naturalization Index, 1907-1995) — indexed + images. John Mogan, if foreign-born, would have a naturalization record naming his residence, age, and sometimes family.

### City directories
- **Availability:** Detroit city directories 1861-1923 on Fold3 ($); Michigan State Gazetteers and Business Directories 1863-1922 on HathiTrust (free). Detroit City Directory 1895 on MyHeritage ($).
- **Research value:** Track household address year-by-year between censuses; can reveal changes in household composition, boarders, or adult children living nearby.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Key collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Births 1867-1917, Deaths 1867-1897, Marriages 1820-1941, Naturalization, Obituaries, Church Records, Census, State Census 1894, Probate (browse-only) | Free |
| Ancestry | Birth Records 1867-1913, Death Records 1867-1952, Marriages, Wills & Probate, City Directories, Census, Newspapers | Subscription |
| Michiganology | Michigan Death Certificates 1897-1952 | Free |
| Chronicling America | Michigan digitized newspapers | Free |
| Fold3 | Detroit City Directories 1861-1923 | Subscription |
| HathiTrust | Michigan State Gazetteers 1863-1922 | Free |
| FindAGrave / BillionGraves | Cemetery records | Free |

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library (5201 Woodward Ave) | Vital records, Wayne County marriage returns 1803-1893, Catholic church microfilm 1704-1930, city directories, probate indexes, family histories, newspapers, Wayne County Death Record Index 1934-1953 | In-person; some finding aids online |
| Wayne County Clerk's Office, Coleman A. Young Municipal Center | Detroit city births (since 1893), marriage and divorce records | In-person / mail |
| Detroit Health Department (1151 Taylor St) | Detroit city deaths since 1897 | In-person / mail |
| Wayne County Probate Court, Coleman A. Young Municipal Center | Probate records for all of Wayne County | In-person |
| Felician Sisters of North America Provincial Archive (Livonia, MI) | Polish Catholic parish/school/orphanage records | Contact: fsnaarchives@feliciansisters.org |

## Records NOT online
- Detroit city birth records before 1893 (pre-registration period); original Detroit city birth records after that at Wayne County Clerk's Office
- Detroit city death records before 1897 at original repositories; microfiche Detroit Death Index 1920–current at Burton Historical Collection (not digitized online)
- Wayne County marriage returns 1803-1893 (originals at Burton Historical Collection)
- Full run of Roman Catholic Archdiocesan church registers on microfilm at Burton Historical Collection only
- Detroit city directory volumes not covered by Fold3 or HathiTrust

## Known record losses
- The 1890 federal census was destroyed by fire and is not available for any US locality.
- Michigan vital records show compliance gaps 1867-1904; some births and deaths during this period were simply never registered.

## Research tips
- **Start with the census enumerations** (1880, 1900, 1910, 1920) to build the complete household picture of the Mogan family across time — any child living at home will appear, and ages of listed children help bracket birth years for targeted vital-record searches.
- **Search FamilySearch Michigan Obituaries first** (col. 2215693) — obituaries for parents and known children often name all siblings, including those who died young or moved away.
- **Irish Catholics in Detroit**: prioritize the Roman Catholic baptismal and burial registers at Burton Historical Collection for events not captured in civil registration, especially births before 1905.
- **Michigan County Births (col. 1923472) excludes Detroit city** — do not rely on it for births occurring within the city limits; use the Ancestry Michigan Birth Records 1867-1913 (index & images) instead, which covers the city.
- **Michigan Death records after 1897** require checking Michiganology (michiganology.org, 1897-1952, organized by county then surname) and Ancestry's Michigan Death Records 1867-1952 for indexed access to death certificates listing parents.
- **Naturalization records**: John Mogan's naturalization petition (if he was foreign-born) may name his wife and children; search col. 2546149 and col. 2110745.
- **Detroit street renumbering (1 January 1921)**: pre-1921 and post-1921 addresses for the same house will differ — do not conclude a different address means a different household.
